text.p: Federal-Mogul Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Dick Snell on Wednesday said he would like the automotive parts maker to complete an acquisition worth "several hundred million dollars" in 1997.

Snell, speaking to reporters after the company's annual shareholders meeting in Southfield, said acquisitions were part of Federal-Mogul's long-term plan to expand and develop its core automotive products manufacturing businesses.
"It's my hope in 1997 that we complete an acquisition that's of some substance," Snell said.
Although he defined such an acquisition as one worth "several hundred million dollars," Snell also the company is also looking at smaller acquisitions in the range of $10 million to $15 million.
He said Federal-Mogul was in preliminary discussions with possible acquisition targets but declined to provide further information.

Snell said Federal-Mogul may be forced to idle workers at its auto parts units if strikes against Chrysler Corp and General Motors Corp continued. So far, Federal-Mogul has not been forced to shut any plants because of the strikes, but that could change if the disputes dragged on for two more weeks.
"At this point, we hope cooler heads will prevail and things will be settled," Snell said.
About 10-15 percent of Federal Mogul's total revenues come from sales to Chrysler, GM and Ford Motor Co, he said.
